body:
Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. ㉠당신은
누군가의 삶에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 뿐만 아니라, 당
신의 경력에 귀중한 기술들도 습득할 수 있다. It even
reduces stress and anxiety. With busy schedules, it
can be hard to find the time to commit to
volunteer work. These days, however, you can make
a huge difference in the lives of others from your
own home by virtually volunteering. Here are a few
ways to virtually volunteer.
First, you could be a part of the effort to lend
support
to
senior
citizens
who
struggle
with
loneliness. (A) Typically, volunteer “phone friends”
make regular calls to chat and check in with these
people. (B) Second, you can help people with low or
no vision with their everyday tasks. (C) Through a
live video call, you can offer visual assistance to
those who need it with tasks such as reading “use
by” dates and instructions on food packages, which
helps them to lead more independent lives. (D) Also,
specialized technology, such as screen readers and
voice-controlled
devices, helps visually impaired
people. (E) Finally, if you have an interest in wildlife
and its conservation, you can help with animal
monitoring work by watching live videos of animal
habitats around the world. Monitoring these animals
helps protect wildlife and develop methods of
conserving them.
Helping others and giving back to the community
can be very rewarding. It can make your day more
meaningful and productive. It is also a great way to
connect with new people and cultures. For those
who believe in karma, if you do good things for
others, good things will happen to you!

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Day 4
I woke up late in the morning and reached for my
phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember
my social media apps were no longer there. Old
habits die (A)[hard / easily]. After breakfast, I felt a
strong urge to go online, which I didn’t want to
(B)[hold back / give in to]. So, I decided to go out
for a walk.
While walking in the park, I probably glanced at
my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at
the people around me, most of whom had their
eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze upward
and noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a
single cloud in sight. All around the park, trees
slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found myself
taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful scene.
After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under
my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I
ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn’t matter
that I’m not really good at it. It just felt great that
I was (C)[lost in / distracted by] doing something
for several hours without getting interrupted by my
phone.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 휴대 전화에 더 이상 소셜 미디어 앱이 없음에도, 일어나 휴대폰을 열어보았으므로, 오랜 습관은 잘 사라지지 않는다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 습관은 쉽게 안 고쳐진다’라는 의 미의 관용 표현을 이루는 hard가 알맞다. (B) 온라인에 접속하고 싶은 강한 충동을 느꼈지만, 이에 굴복 하고 싶지 않아 산책을 나갔다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로, ‘~에 굴복하다‘의 의미를 갖는 give in to가 알맞다. (C) 결국 오후 내내 기타를 치게 되었으므로, 휴대 전화에 방 해 받지 않고 여러 시간 동안 뭔가에 ‘몰두했다’는 흐름이 되 어야 하므로 lost in(~에 몰두한)이 알맞다.

body:
Day 7
I don’t know why, but today I momentarily
(A)[tighten up / let down] my guard against social
media. As if bound by a spell, I logged into one of
the social media sites, only to find that there was
nothing interesting. I had a weird feeling of being
at a place where I didn’t belong, which was quickly
replaced by a sense of ⓐ_________. I really shouldn’t
have gone back to a social media site in the middle
of my detox.
Day 11
This was the first day my phone felt more like a
brick in my pocket than a digital device. I could
already feel (B)[bound by / free from] worrying
about posting something and hoping it would get
some likes. At a gathering with my friends, it was
fun to get asked over and over again about how I
was surviving without social media. Sam said, “I
don’t think I could give up social media for even
one day.” My immediate thought was: Then you
really need to give it up! I didn’t actually say that,
although I wanted to.
Day 14
Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my
social media break and what things had been like
before. I realized that social media had taken some
control of me. It’s kind of ⓑ____________ that all I
did was envy others for their perfectly happy
moments in life, dress up my everyday events, and
think up ways to get others to like my posts.
From now on, I want to be in control of how I
use something or do something, not the other way
around. Tomorrow, I will return to my social media
activities, but in more careful and controlled ways.
I’m going to stick to just a couple of sites that I
really need, while making absolutely sure that my
activities
are
in
(C)[line
/
conflict]
with
my
well-being and happiness.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)

solution: (A) 디톡스 중에 소셜 미디어에 로그인 했으므로, 경계를 ‘풀다, 느슨하게 하다’라는 뜻을 이루는 ‘let down'이 알맞다. (B) 열한 번째 날은 휴대 전화가 벽돌처럼 느껴지기 시작한 첫 번째 날이라고 했으므로, 뭔가를 올리는 데 대해 고민하고 ‘좋 아요’를 좀 받을 것을 바라는 것으로부터 ‘자유로워’졌다는 흐 름의 ‘free from'이 알맞다. (C) 2주간의 디톡스를 마치며 다짐하는 내용으로, 앞으로 자신 의 소셜 미디어 활동이 확실히 내 웰빙과 행복에 ’연관되도록‘ 할 것이라는 흐름이 자연스러우므로 ’line'이 알맞다.

(A)
(B)

solution: (A) 누군가의 삶에 긍정적인 영향을 미치며, 귀중한 기술도 습 득할 수 있고 스트레스와 불안도 줄여준다는 이점들이 이어지 고 있으므로 benefits(이점들)가 알맞다. (B) 실시간 화상 통화를 통해, 식품 포장의 사용 기한 및 사용 법을 읽어주는 것은 시력이 낮거나 시력을 잃은 사람들이 일 상적인 활동을 할 수 있도록 도움을 주는 것이므로, 그들이 더 '독립적인(independent)' 삶을 살 수 있도록 도와준다는 흐름이 알맞다. (C) 자원 봉사 활동을 장려하는 글로, 다른 사람을 돕고 지역 사회에 환원하는 것이 의미 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, rewarding(보람 있는)이 알맞다.

body:
Day 1
So it was time to pull the plug.
I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared
at the social media icons dotting the screen. I
(A)[derived / removed] the apps from my phone.
Then I moved to my notebook computer. I logged
out of all of the social media sites. I felt an
immediate sense of relief.
But soon after, I got (B)[restless / relieved]. I don’t
remember how long it was, but I stared at my
phone screen in complete confusion for quite a
while. I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an
hour. But there’s only so much you can do over a
voice call. We decided to meet later in the
afternoon for a bike ride.
What else can I do on my phone? I lay on my
bed even though I wasn’t sleepy. I stayed there
until I went out to meet Jamie. Throughout the
day, it felt like things slowed down considerably.
What a (C)[short / long] day!

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 플러그를 뽑을 시간이라는 말로 시작하여, 소셜 미디어 사 이트에서 로그아웃하였다는 내용이 이어지므로, 필자가 소셜 미디어 사용을 줄이기(디톡스하기) 위해 자신의 휴대전화에서 앱들을 ‘삭제했다(removed)'는 흐름이 알맞다. (B) 소셜 미디어 사이트에서 로그아웃한 즉시 안도감을 느꼈다는 앞 단락의 내용과 대조되는 But으로 이어지고 있으므로, 안도 감과 반대인 ’안절부절 못하는(restless)‘ 상태라는 흐름이 알맞다 (C) 하루 내내 시간이 상당히 더디게 간 것 같았다는 앞 내용에 이어지고 있으므로, 정말 ’긴(long)‘ 하루였다는 흐름이 알맞다.

body:
Part 1 FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)
“Selena. SELENA!”
“Yes,” I look up from my phone to discover my
mom yelling at me. She seems to be searching for
an answer to something. “What?” I asked.
She asked, “Did you not hear what I just said?”
No, I didn’t. I didn’t hear anything she said. I
usually don’t hear a single word (A)[saying / said]
to me by anyone. And why is that? It’s because my
eyes are fixed on my phone. My mom always asks
me, “What is so interesting on your phone?” I
never know how to answer that because even I
don’t know what’s so interesting on my phone.
I have a bad case of anxiety ⓐ_____________________
_____________________________. I spend most of my day
on social media. I fear missing out on social media.
I fear not being in the know of (B)[that / what]
everyone is discussing. I fear not being in the know
of what my friends are posting on social media.
My mom thinks I’m addicted to my phone. Older
people think teenagers like me have an addiction
to their phones and computers. But I wouldn’t say
it’s an addiction to a device. It’s an addiction to
social media. It’s an addiction to being online, or in
other words, a fear of not being online.
Basically, I have severe FOMO, for (C)[what / which]
I’m in desperate need of a cure. Maybe this spring
break could be a chance to find one.

(C) 주절에 콤마로 연결되어 있고, 뒤에 완전한 절(I‘m in desperate need of a cure)이 이어지고 있으므로, 접속사 역할 을 하면서 완전한 절을 이끌 수 있는 ’전치사+관계대명사‘의 형태가 되어야 한다. 이때 관계대명사 what은 완전한 절을 이 끌 수 없으므로, which가 알맞다.

Part 2 My Two-week Detox
Day 4
I woke up late in the morning and reached for my
phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember
my social media apps were no longer there.
_______________________________________. After breakfast,
I felt a strong urge to go online, to which I didn’t
want to give in. So, I decided to go out for a walk.
While walking in the park, I probably glanced at
my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at
the people around me, most of whom had their
eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze
upward and noticed how purely blue the sky was,
without a single cloud in sight. All around the park,
trees slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found
myself taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful
scene.
After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under
my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I
ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn’t matter
that I’m not really good at it. It just felt great that
I was lost in doing something for several hours
without getting interrupted by my phone.

윗글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Taking a walk in the park can make peoplehealthier and happier.
The writer was concerned about smartphoneaddiction in herself and others.
The writer could easily find people who often spendtoo much time on their phones and social media.
Playing musical instruments is a better way toenhance concentration than avoiding social media.
By breaking free from social media, the writercould enjoy nature and playing the guitar withoutdistractions.

Part 2 My Two-week Detox
Day 1
So it was time to pull the plug.
I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared
at the social media icons dotting the screen. I
removed the apps from my phone. Then I moved
to my notebook computer. I logged out of all of
the social media sites. I felt an immediate sense of
relief.

how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen
in complete confusion for quite a while. I called
Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour. But
there’s only so much you can do over a voice call.
We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a
bike ride.
What else can I do on my phone? I lay on my
bed even though I wasn’t sleepy. I stayed there
until I went out to meet Jamie. Throughout the
day, it felt like things slowed down considerably.
What a long day!

The writer immediately felt anxious after removingthe apps.
The writer stared at her phone screen for quitea while in confusion.
Later in the afternoon, the writer arranged toride bikes with Jamie.
After the call with Jamie, the writer spent thewhole time in bed until she went out.

Part 1 FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)
“Selena. SELENA!”
“Yes,” I look up from my phone to discover my
mom yelling at me. She seems to be searching for
an answer to something. “What?” I asked.
She asked, “Did you not hear what I just said?”
No, I didn’t. I didn’t hear anything she said. I
usually don’t hear a single word (A)[saying / said]
to me by anyone. And why is that? It’s because my
eyes are fixed on my phone. My mom always asks
me, “What is so interesting on your phone?” I
never know how to answer that because even I
don’t know what’s so interesting on my phone.
I have a bad case of anxiety ⓐ_____________________
_____________________________. I spend most of my day
on social media. I fear missing out on social media.
I fear not being in the know of (B)[that / what]
everyone is discussing. I fear not being in the know
of what my friends are posting on social media.
My mom thinks I’m addicted to my phone. Older
people think teenagers like me have an addiction
to their phones and computers. But I wouldn’t say
it’s an addiction to a device. It’s an addiction to
social media. It’s an addiction to being online, or in
other words, a fear of not being online.
Basically, I have severe FOMO, for (C)[what / which]
I’m in desperate need of a cure. Maybe this spring
break could be a chance to find one.

윗글의 ‘I’에 대한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: I couldn't hear what my mom said because Iwas completely focused on my phone.
I feel nervous about not keeping up with theissues everyone is talking about.
I'm afraid of missing my friends' posts on socialmedia.
Contrary to what my mom thinks, I’m addictedto the device itself, not to being online.
I think I need a treatment for severe FOMO andI’ll try to find one during spring break.

Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. ㉠당신은

can be hard to find the time to commit to
volunteer work. These days, however, you can make
a huge difference in the lives of others from your
own home by virtually volunteering. Here are a few
ways to virtually volunteer.
First, you could be a part of the effort to lend
support
to
senior
citizens
who
struggle
with
loneliness. (A) Typically, volunteer “phone friends”
make regular calls to chat and check in with these
people. (B) Second, you can help people with low or
no vision with their everyday tasks. (C) Through a
live video call, you can offer visual assistance to
those who need it with tasks such as reading “use

helps them to lead more independent lives. (D) Also,

voice-controlled
devices, helps visually impaired

meaningful and productive. It is also a great way to

others, good things will happen to you!

body:
Fun Shadows
When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. He lets his creativity flow to make
beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.
His playful shadow art illustrations are made by
ⓐadding his own doodles to shadows cast from
everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. In one
image, the shadow from a key is reinterpreted as a
DJ wearing headphones. In another, a potato peeler
creates the perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In
his art, the shadow from a glass becomes a pool.
He uses a very simple process to draw his
pictures. ㉠그 과정을 시작하기 위해, 그가 할 필요가
있는 일은 평범한 물건, 종이 한 장, 그리고 조명을 준
비하는 것뿐이다. Then he puts the object on the
paper and turns on the light. He just starts moving
the light around and places the object in different
positions. He keeps a very (A)[open / closed] mind
and tries not to have an idea in advance about
what the result should be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create ⓑwhatever I want,” he says. His free
artistic interpretation of shadows means that the
possibilities for creating new doodles are (B)[endless
/ restricted].
In fact, it was by accident ⓒwhich he started
making his art pieces. While he was working on a
new script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of
a cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. He
completed the image with a few lines, took a
picture and shared it on the Internet. The reactions
were so positive that he challenged ⓓhim to make
one shadow image every day.
Art can inspire you to see the world from a(n)
(C)[new / existing] angle. Connecting ideas that at
first glance appear ⓔunrelated is a powerful tool
for exploring the beauty of the world around us. To
make such connections, all you need is your
imaginative power.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 미리 특정한 결과를 정해두는 것이 아니고 무언가가 보일 때까지 물건들을 만지작거린다고 언급하고 있으므로, '열린 (open)' 마음을 유지한다는 흐름이 알맞다. (B) 자신이 원하는 것은 무엇이든 만들어 낼 수 있다고 말하는 Vincent Bal의 그림자에 대한 자유로운 예술적 해석이 언급되 고 있으므로, 새로운 낙서를 만들 가능성이 ‘무한한(endless)'이 흐름상 알맞다. (C) 상상력을 통해 관련이 없어 보이는 아이디어를 연결하는 예술에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 예술이 '새로운(new)' 각도로 세상을 보도록 영감을 준다는 흐름이 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 2과

Beyond the Scene
Meet Robin Yayla, a visual storyteller living in Milan,
Italy, who has been delighting his viewers with his

on top of photos of landmarks or buildings and

finding whatever is common in two unrelated things,
he connects them smoothly in his digital drawing.

body:
Surprising Connection
Paintings of Rob Gonsalves, a Canadian magic
realist artist, combine two different points of view.
They give the viewer the visual illusion that they
are looking at two unrelated realities flawlessly
(A)[fused / divided] in one painting. They usually
depict landscapes and objects that ⓐseem to
change from one thing to another.
When you look at the top right corner of the
painting above, you can see a kid jumping on his
bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the
bedcovers change into fields, ⓑwhich a girl now
appears to be flying. This is how the visual illusion
is created: an object is gradually changed through a
series of similar shapes into something entirely
(B)[identical / different] in a single scene. At the
same time, two different parts of the same scene
are constructed at different scales. The result is an
unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.
This kind of illusion has a fun way of ⓒtwisting
your perception. It makes you question what is real.
Most of his incredible paintings have a(n) (C)[clear /
unclear] boundary between the multiple stories they
tell, which forces the viewer ⓓto jump back and
forth between them. ⓔTrace the transitions, you get
that delightful “Ah-ha!” feeling as you try to decide
exactly where one world transforms into another.

(B)
(C)
solution: (A) Rob Gonsalves의 그림은 두 가지 다른 관점을 결합한다고 언급했으므로, 하나의 그림에 완벽하게 ‘융합된(fused)’ 서로 관 련 없는 두 현실을 보고 있다는 흐름이 알맞다. (B) 한 장면에서 침대보가 들판으로 변하므로, 비슷한 형체들이 완전히 ‘다른(different)' 어떤 것으로 변한다는 흐름이 알맞다. (C) 관람객이 이야기 사이를 이리저리 뛰어넘어 다닐 수 있도 록 하고, 정확히 어디에서 다른 세계로 바뀌는지 판정하려고 애쓴다는 내용이 이어지므로, 그림들이 들려주는 이야기들 사 이에 ’불분명한(unclear)‘ 경계가 있다는 흐름이 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 2과

He uses a very ㉠[simple / complex] process to
draw his pictures. To start the process, all he needs
to do is prepare a plain object, a piece of paper,
and a light. Then he puts the object on the paper
and turns on the light. He just starts moving the
light around and places the object in different
positions. He keeps a very open mind and tries not
to have an idea in advance about what the result
should be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create whatever I want,” he says. His ㉡[free /
controlled] artistic interpretation of shadows means
that the possibilities for creating new doodles are
endless.
In fact, it was ㉢[by accident / on purpose] that
he started making his art pieces. While he was
working on a new script, he suddenly noticed how
the shadow of a cup on his desk looked like a
little elephant. He completed the image with a few
lines, took a picture and shared it on the Internet.

To breathe life into well-known structures around the world, he often uses iconic pop culture characters. His unique twists sometimes turn what we consider dull and boring into something delightful. To him, a bridge is a net, and a road is a bowling lane. After finding whatever is common in two unrelated things, he connects them smoothly in his digital drawing. His playful shadow art illustrations are made by adding his own doodles to shadows cast from everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book

Greene classic I had brought back from my trip and

into
graphic
shapes,
which
ended
up
resembling my cat, and it turned out to be a
unique composition.

Fun Shadows
When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. He lets his creativity ⓐto flow to
make beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.
His playful shadow art illustrations are made ㉠____
__________________________________________________________,
like a flower or a glass. In one image, the shadow
from a key is reinterpreted as a DJ ⓑwearing
headphones. In another, a potato peeler creates the
perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In his art, the
shadow from a glass becomes a pool.
He uses a very simple process to draw his
pictures. To start the process, all he needs to do is
ⓒprepare a plain object, a piece of paper, and a
light. Then he puts the object on the paper and
turns on the light. He just starts moving the light
around and places the object in different positions.
He keeps a very open mind and tries not to have
an idea in advance about what the result should
be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create whatever I want,” he says. His free
artistic interpretation of shadows means that the
possibilities for creating new doodles are endless.

연한 일이었다. While he was working on a new
script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of a
cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. He
completed the image with a few lines, took a
picture and shared it on the Internet. The reactions
were so positive ⓓwhat he challenged himself to
make one shadow image every day.
Art can inspire you to see the world from a new
angle. ⓔConnecting ideas that at first glance
appear unrelated is a powerful tool for exploring
the beauty of the world around us. To make such
connections, all you need is your imaginative power.

Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book
with beautiful notes written in it. That got me

Feeling sad, I found myself picking up the Graham
Greene classic I had brought back from my trip and
___________________________________________. I then hung

everything for the sculpture is made from the
pages
within
that
book;
some
don’t
have

representations of the narratives and the characters.

Surprising Connection
Paintings of Rob Gonsalves, a Canadian magic
realist artist, combine two different points of view.
They give the viewer the visual illusion that they
are looking at ⓐ_______________________________________
__________________ They usually depict landscapes and
objects that seem to change from one thing to
another.
When you look at the top right corner of the
painting above, you can see a kid jumping on his
bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the
bedcovers change into fields, which a girl now
appears to be flying over. This is (A)[how / what]
the visual illusion is created: an object is gradually
changed through a series of similar shapes into
something entirely different in a single scene. At
the same time, two different parts of the same
scene are constructed at different scales. The result
is an unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.
This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your
perception. It makes you question what is real.
Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear
boundary between the multiple stories they tell,

and forth between them. (C)[Tracing / Traced] the
transitions, you get that delightful “Ah-ha!” feeling

transforms into another.

When we look at shadows of objects in real life,
most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist
and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them
into art forms. (A) He lets his creativity flow to
make
beautiful
and
meaningful
scenes
with
shadows. (B)
His playful shadow art illustrations are made by
adding his own doodles to shadows cast from
everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. (C) In
another, a potato peeler creates the perfectly
shaped frame for a piano. (D) In his art, the
shadow from a glass becomes a pool. (E)
He uses a very ㉠[simple / complex] process to
draw his pictures. To start the process, all he needs
to do is prepare a plain object, a piece of paper,
and a light. Then he puts the object on the paper
and turns on the light. He just starts moving the
light around and places the object in different
positions. He keeps a very open mind and tries not
to have an idea in advance about what the result
should be.
“If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it
always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take
another object, and then I just start playing around
with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I
can create whatever I want,” he says. His ㉡[free /
controlled] artistic interpretation of shadows means
that the possibilities for creating new doodles are
endless.
In fact, it was ㉢[by accident / on purpose] that
he started making his art pieces. While he was
working on a new script, he suddenly noticed how
the shadow of a cup on his desk looked like a
little elephant. He completed the image with a few
lines, took a picture and shared it on the Internet.

coconut curry.

nature and a great ⓐalternative source of vitamins,
proteins, and minerals. Not only full of nutrients,

precious land space as they are grown in water.

lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing
of light and the nutrients in the water supply are all
controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is able
to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year round.
Vertical farming refers to producing foods in
vertically
stacked
layers
integrated
into
other
structures, usually without the need of soil or
natural light. Since the plants are stacked above
each other, it (A)[cuts / increases] the amount of
space needed to grow crops.
Another (B)[advantage / disadvantage] of indoor
vertical
farming
is
that
maintaining
the
ideal
conditions can reduce the time to harvest. “For
traditional farming, if the climate is good, you have
five to six harvests a year,” says the manager of the
facility. “In indoor farming, we’re now getting
roughly 17 harvests out of that same period.”
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for
water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb
will drop down to the plants below. The manager
says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in
a field. “Every time water moves through the
system, it’s captured and reused.”
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles’
heel: energy consumption. It has been (C)[praised /
criticized] for the high energy input it requires.
“Solar power could help bring down energy costs,”
the manager says. “Large scale farms will have solar
panels on each roof. It might support 10 to 15% of
our needs.”
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather
than replace outside fields. “Much of our fruit and
vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in
soil, which is why it is super important that we also
invest in sustainable field farming,” the manager says.

(B) 앞에서 (실내) 수직 농업의 이점으로 공간의 양을 줄인다고 했으며, 이상적인 조건을 유지하는 것이 수확까지 걸리는 시간 을 줄일 수 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, 실내 수직 농업의 또 다른 이점이라는 흐름이 되는 advantage(장점)가 알맞다. (C) 앞에서 실내 수직 농업에는 에너지 소비라는 약점이 있다 고 했으므로, 그것이 요구하는 높은 에너지 투입에 대해 비난 받아 왔다는 흐름이 되는 criticized(비난받는)가 알맞다.

3D food printing has the potential to save the
environment, while (A)[revolutionizing / revolutionized]
food
production; for example, it can
convert
alternative ingredients such as proteins from insects
into delicious meals. The underlying concept for
food printing is the same as any other 3D printing.
In 3D food printing, various inks ― liquid forms of
food ― are placed one layer at a time to build
complex 3D constructs with full textures and
(B)[customizing / customized] nutrients.
3D food printing can be readily undertaken in
many parts of the globe. Various food inks with
adequate nutrients and favorable flavors can be
sent to areas that are hard to get to, (C)[which /
where] food can be printed on site. In this way, 3D
printed food with necessary nutrients can be
provided for large populations in areas affected by
a natural disaster or a crisis developed by humans.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)               (B)            (C)
solution: (A) 시간 관계를 분명히 하기 위해 접속사 while을 남겨둔 ‘접 속사+분사 ~’ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절 주어와 일치하는 분사구문의 의미상 주어 3D food printing이 ‘혁신을 일으키는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 food production이 있으므로, 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 revolutionizing이 알맞다. (B) 전치사 with의 첫 번째 목적어인 명사구 full textures와 등 위접속사 and로 명사구가 병렬연결을 이루어야 하므로 ‘맞춤 형의’라는 뜻으로 명사 nutrients를 수식하는 과거분사 형태의 형용사 customized가 알맞다. (C) 쉼표(,) 뒤에서 완전한 절(food ~ on site)을 이끌어 선행사 인 명사구 areas that are hard to get to를 부연 설명하는 관 계사절을 이루고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 관계부사 where가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat obtained by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies show that (A)[produce / producing] lab-grown meat by using renewable energy would have a significantly lower carbon footprint than raising farm animals and making meat products in the most sustainable way. This is how lab-grown meat is made. (B)[To begin / Beginning] with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number of cells from an animal. Then, they multiply and grow the harvested cells, and they produce real tissue, which is quite similar to conventional meat in terms of texture and smell. In this way, lab-grown cells can (C)[transform / be transformed] into steak, chicken breasts, or hamburger meat. The final product itself is a real cut of meat, ready to be cooked.
solution:
1. (A) that절에서 동사 would have의 주어가 되는 명사구가 와야 하므로 동명사 producing이 알맞다(동사원형 produce는 주어가 될 수 없다).
2. (B) 쉼표와 함께 ‘우선, 먼저’를 뜻하는 독립부정사 To begin with를 이루므로 To begin이 알맞다.
3. (C) 실험실 세포는 과학자들에 의해 스테이크 등으로 ‘바뀌는’ 대상이므로 transform A into B의 수동형 be transformed가 알맞다.
4. (A) producing, (B) To begin, (C) be transformed를 모두 갖춘 것은 ③뿐이다.
5. 따라서 답은 ③이다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때,알맞지 않은 것은?

Food is the essence of life as it fuels us, ⓐbrings
us together, and connects communities to their
cultures. What and how we eat is also crucial in
sustaining all life on this planet.
According to the UN population prospects report,
by 2050, the global population is expected to
increase to around 10 billion. This means that, to
feed everyone, it will take 56% more food than is
produced in the world today. Unfortunately, there is
not ⓑenough agricultural land available to provide
larger future populations with the kinds of diet
people are eating in most countries today.
In addition to this, industrial food systems generate
more than one third of all greenhouse gas emissions.
ⓒThe processes we rely on to produce, transport,
and store meals and raw ingredients, not to
mention ⓓthe landfills covered with food waste, are
speeding up climate change. Animal-based foods,
including red meat, milk products, and farmed
shrimp, are generally associated with the highest
greenhouse gas emissions. Especially, our meat
production accelerates global warming significantly,
uses shrinking supplies of fresh water, destroys
forests and grasslands, and damages soil.
Basically, we are in a tight bind of our own
making. Against this reality, it is vital for us to seek
sustainable alternatives to our current diets. Let us
explore ⓔsome ways we could be eating in the
near future.
choices: ⓑ: enough agricultural land that is available
ⓒ: The processes on which we rely
ⓓ: the landfills that are covered with food waste
ⓔ: some ways in which we could be eating

solution: (A) 문장의 동사로 reduces가 쓰였으므로 흐름상 앞의 명사 (space)를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하 며, space(공간)가 ‘필요하게 되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 needed가 알맞다. (B) 완전한 절(the farm ~ field)을 이끌어 동사 says의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사로 쓰이며, 불완전한 절을 이끌어 문장에서 주어, 목적어, 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이룬다. (C) ‘~하는 데 도움이 되다, ~하는 것을 돕다’라는 뜻으로 ‘help+동사원형/to부정사’를 쓸 수 있으므로, could help 뒤에 to부정사인 to bring이 알맞다.

Perfectly ⓐshaped tomatoes grow under purple
lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing
of light and the nutrients in the water supply are
all controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is
able to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year

Vertical farming refers to ⓑproduce foods in
vertically
stacked
layers
integrated
into
other
structures, usually without the need of soil or
natural light. Since the plants are stacked above
each other, it reduces the amount of space needed
to grow crops.
ⓒOther advantage of indoor vertical farming is
that maintaining the ideal conditions can reduce the
time to harvest. “For traditional farming, if the
climate is good, you have five to six harvests a
year,” says the manager of the facility. “In indoor
farming, we’re now getting roughly 17 harvests out
of that same period.”
There is also the benefit of a reduced need for
water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb
will drop down to the plants below. The manager
says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in
a field. “ⓓEvery time water moves through the
system, it’s captured and reused.”
However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles’
heel: energy consumption. It ⓔhas criticized for the
high energy input it requires. “Solar power could
help bring down energy costs,” the manager says.
“Large scale farms will have solar panels on each
roof. It might support 10 to 15% of our needs.”
This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather
than replace outside fields. “Much of our fruit and
vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in
soil, ⓕthat is why it is super important that we also
invest in sustainable field farming,” the manager
says.

Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a
laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat obtained
by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies
show that producing lab-grown meat by using
renewable energy would have a significantly lower
carbon footprint than raising farm animals and
making meat products in the most sustainable way.
This is how lab-grown meat is made. To begin
with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number
of cells from an animal. Then, they multiply and
grow the harvested cells, and they produce real
tissue, which is quite similar to conventional meat
in terms of texture and smell. In this way, they can
transform lab-grown cells into steak, chicken breasts,
or hamburger meat. The final product itself is a real
cut of meat, ready to be cooked.

global

3D food printing has the potential to save the
environment, while revolutionizing food production;
for example, it can convert alternative ingredients
such as proteins from insects into delicious meals.
The underlying concept for food printing is the
same as any other 3D printing. In 3D food printing,
various inks ― liquid forms of food ― are placed
one layer at a time to build complex 3D constructs
with full textures and customized nutrients.
3D food printing can be readily undertaken in
many parts of the globe. Various food inks with
adequate nutrients and favorable flavors can be
sent to areas that are hard to get to, where food
can be printed on site. In this way, 3D printed food
with necessary nutrients can be provided for large
populations in areas affected by a natural disaster
or a crisis developed by humans.

Food is the essence of life as it fuels us, brings us
together, and connects communities to their cultures.
What and how we eat is also crucial in sustaining
all life on this planet.
According to the UN population prospects report,
by 2050, the global population is expected to
increase to around 10 billion. (A)이는, 모든 사람을
먹여 살리기 위해, 오늘날 세계에서 생산되는 것보다
56% 더 많은 식량이 필요할 것이라는 것을 의미한다.
Unfortunately, there is not enough agricultural land
available to provide larger future populations with
the kinds of diet people are eating in most
countries today.
In addition to this, industrial food systems generate
more than one third of all greenhouse gas emissions.
(B)음식물 쓰레기로 뒤덮인 매립지는 말할 것도 없고,
우리가 음식과 원재료를 생산, 운송, 보관하기 위해 의

and farmed shrimp, are generally associated with

our meat production accelerates global warming
significantly, uses shrinking supplies of fresh water,
destroys forests and grasslands, and damages soil.

(A)곤충을 먹는다는 것이 몇몇 사람들에게는 이상해
보일 수 있지만, 그것들은 오랫동안 인간의 식단의 한
부분이었다. In fact, insect eating is practiced in
about 130 countries!
Insects will be ⓐinsignificant in the fight against
hunger and climate change. They use much fewer
resources than farm animals to produce the same
amount of protein and can be raised on food
waste, which makes raising them very ⓑcost-
effective.
The main ⓒbarrier to using insects as a source of
protein is the negative image they have. Insects are
associated with disease and dirt, so manufacturers
of insect food products must overcome this to
successfully win the public over. One solution has
been to change the ⓓlook of the insects, by drying
and grinding them into powder. Rich in protein,
insect flour is gaining popularity as a healthier
replacement for wheat flour. In addition, insect oils
are an ⓔunsuccessful field; they are already being
used in some parts of the world for cooking.

다음 글의 제목을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (각 빈칸에 한 단 어씩 쓰고, 각 단어의 첫 철자는 대문자로 쓸 것)

Perfectly shaped tomatoes grow under purple lighting. Here in the facility, the intensity and timing of light and the nutrients in the water supply are all controlled. This indoor vertical farming facility is able to produce fresh fruit and vegetables all year round. Vertical farming refers to producing foods in vertically stacked layers integrated into other structures, usually without the need of soil or natural light. Since the plants are stacked above each other, it reduces the amount of space needed to grow crops. Another advantage of indoor vertical farming is that maintaining the ideal conditions can reduce the time to harvest. “For traditional farming, if the climate is good, you have five to six harvests a year,” says the manager of the facility. “In indoor farming, we’re now getting roughly 17 harvests out of that same period.” There is also the benefit of a reduced need for water. Any excess water that a plant cannot absorb will drop down to the plants below. The manager says the farm uses 95% less water than farming in a field. “Every time water moves through the system, it’s captured and reused.” However, indoor vertical farming has an Achilles’ heel: energy consumption. It has been criticized for the high energy input it requires. “Solar power could help bring down energy costs,” the manager says. “Large scale farms will have solar panels on each roof. It might support 10 to 15% of our needs.” This farm wants to fill supply chain gaps rather than replace outside fields. “Much of our fruit and vegetables will still be grown under the sun and in soil, which is why it is super important that we also invest in sustainable field farming,” the manager says. ______________ ______________ ______________: More Produce, Less ______________, Time and ______________, Yet Higher ______________ Use 천재(강상구) 3과
answer: Indoor Vertical Farming : Space[Water] Water[Space] Energy

Weidensaul: To find their routes, the bar-tailed
godwits probably rely on the sun and stars
among other things. Some experts believe that
they may be able to sense the earth’s magnetic
field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if
ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean.

body:
Jo: How do they travel such a long distance over a nearly (A)featureless ocean?
Weidensaul: To find their routes, the bar-tailed godwits probably rely on the sun and stars among other things. Some experts believe that they may be able to (B)sense the earth’s magnetic field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean. It turns out that migratory birds use an (C)approach called “half-brain sleep.” This is how it works. Only the left half of the brain sleeps for a couple of seconds, then only the right half for the next couple of seconds, and then this process repeats over and over again. Isn’t it amazing? Actually, some sea (D)mammals like dolphins can do that, too, because they have to keep breathing (E)consciously.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): having no interesting parts to notice
(B): to become aware of something even though you cannot see it, hear it, etc.
(C): a road, path, etc. that leads to a place, and is the main way of reaching it
(D): any animal that gives birth to live young, not eggs, and feeds its young on milk
(E): in a way that shows that you are aware of or noticing something
solution:
1. (C) approach는 여기서 '방법, 접근법'(a method of doing something)이라는 뜻으로 쓰였다.
2. 보기 ③의 풀이 '어떤 장소로 이어지는 주된 길'은 approach의 다른 뜻인 '진입로'이다.
3. (A) featureless, (B) sense, (D) mammal, (E) consciously의 풀이는 문맥에 맞다.
따라서 답은 ③이다.

body:
Jo: Hello, listeners. ⓐ여러분은 밤에 여러분 머리 바
로 위로 대규모 이동이 일어날 때가 있다는 것을
아셨나요? The scale of migration involving
billions of birds traveling up to thousands of
kilometers leaves you in (A)[awe / boredom]. On
today’s Jo’s Tea Time, we invite naturalist and
author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge.
He’s spent decades studying migratory birds,
writing
about
them,
and
engaging
in
conservation efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr.
Weidensaul.
Weidensaul: Thanks for having me, Jo.
Jo: Your new book says every spring and fall,
hundreds of millions to billions of migratory
birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to
have no idea that it’s happening. Why is that?
Weidensaul: Well, most birds migrate after dark,
including almost all of the birds that are
normally active during the day. That’s why it’s
(B)[easy / hard] for us to realize the migration is
happening. They migrate at night because the
night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides,
there are (C)[fewer / more] predators at night. If
you could strip away the night sky and make
everything visible, this migration would probably
be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the
planet.
Jo: Among those global travelers in your book, I
found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly
impressive.
Weidensaul: Sure. Some of them can even make a
10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific
Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in
11 days.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 수십억 마리의 새들이 수천 킬로미터까지 여행하는 철새 이동의 규모에 대한 감상이므로, 그것이 경외감을 자아낸다는 흐름이 되는 awe(경외감)가 알맞다. (B) 보통 낮에 활동하는 거의 모든 새를 포함하여 대부분의 새 들이 어두워진 후에 이동한다고 했으므로, 이것의 결과로서 우 리가 이런 이동이 일어난다는 걸 알아차리기 어렵다는 흐름이 되는 hard(어려운)가 알맞다. (C) 새들이 밤에 이동하는 것은 밤하늘이 더 시원하고 공기가 더 잔잔하기 때문이라는 내용 다음에 접속부사 Besides(게다 가)에 연결된 추가적인 이유가 이어져야 하므로, 밤에는 포식 자도 더 적다는 흐름이 되는 fewer(더 적은)가 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 4과

G: Hey, did you watch the nature documentary the
teacher recommended?
B: You mean the one about the endangered
species around us? No, I didn’t. Was it good?
G: Yes, it was. I was particularly impressed by the
part about the Eurasian otters.
B: Oh, you mean the long, thin creatures that like
water? I heard they are very intelligent, playful,
and excellent at catching fish.
G: They sure are. They can swim at the speed of 12
kilometers per hour and dive as deep as 14 meters.
B: That’s cool. But why are they endangered?
G: In the past, they were hunted for their expensive
fur and skin. Nowadays, the bigger threat is the
loss of their habitats due to human activities.
B: What a shame! Shouldn’t we do something
about it?
G: Fortunately, thanks to conservation efforts, their
population is now recovering and more and
more are being spotted around us.
B: Oh, (A)that’s a relief.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: that’s a weight off my mind
solution: 밑줄 친 (A) ‘that’s a relief’는 ‘다행이다’라는 뜻으로, 멸종 위기에 처해 있던 유라시아 수달이 현재는 개체 수가 회복되고 있다는 소녀의 말 을 듣고 다행이라는 뜻의 안도감을 나타내는 의미로 쓰였으므로, 유감 을 나타내는 ❸ ‘that’s too bad(안됐다)’와는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘That’s a relief.’는 ‘I’m relieved.(나는 안심이 된다.)’, ‘What a relief!(정 말 다행이다!)’, ‘I’m glad to hear that.(나는 그 말을 들으니 기쁘다.)’ ‘That’s a weight off my mind.(안심이다.)’ 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding
in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try to
see some hamsters because this is one of the
(A)[best / worst] times of day to see them. At this
time of the day, there’s nobody around so they don’t
have to avoid people while looking for food. These
little ones have been in the area for decades, but
now live among the dead because development has
robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how it is
trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack a
quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks,
which
helps
them
get
through
the
winter.
Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and
flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is (B)[easy /
hard] to find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful
eye, as predators are never too far away. ⓐ그들은
재빨리 굴속으로 도망쳐야 할 수도 있는데, 그것은 땅

urban
areas
generally
having
a
(C)[positive
/

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

G: Hey, did you watch the nature documentary the
teacher recommended?
B:
You mean the ⓐone about the endangered
species around us? No, I didn’t. Was it good?
G: Yes, it was. I was particularly impressed by the
part about the Eurasian otters.
B: Oh, you mean the long, thin creatures ⓑthat
like water? I heard they are very intelligent,
playful, and excellent at catching fish.
G: They ⓒsure are. They can swim at the speed of
12 kilometers per hour and dive as ⓓdeep as
14 meters.
B: That’s cool. But why are they endangered?
G: In the past, they were hunted for their expensive
fur and skin. Nowadays, the bigger threat is the
loss of their habitats due to human activities.
B: ⓔHow a shame! Shouldn’t we do something
about it?
G: Fortunately, thanks to conservation efforts, their
population is now recovering and more and
more are ⓕspotting around us.
B: Oh, that’s a relief.
solution: ⓔ How → What (뒤에 관사 a와 명사 shame이 이어지므로, ‘What+a(n)(+형용사)+명사(구)(+주어+동사)!’ 형태의 감탄문이 되도록 How를 What으로 고친다. 참고로, How가 이끄는 감탄 문은 ‘How+형용사/부사(+주어+동사)’의 구조로 나타낸다.) ⓕ spotting → being spotted (등위접속사 and로 연결되는 절 에 앞의 절(their population is now recovering)과 마찬가지로 현재 진행 중인 일을 나타내는 현재진행형(be동사+현재분사) 이 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주어인 more and more(점점 더 많 은 것들)가 ‘발견되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 목적어 없이 부사구 around us만 이어지고 있으므로, 앞의 be동사 are와 함께 현 재진행 수동태(be동사+being+p.p.)를 이루도록 being spotted 로 고친다.)

body:
Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding
in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try to
see some hamsters because this is one of the best
times of day to see them. At this time of the day,
there’s nobody around so they don’t have to avoid
people while (A)[looked / looking] for food. These
little ones have been in the area for decades, but
now live among the dead because development has
robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how (B)[is
it / it is] trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters
can pack a quarter of their body weight inside their
cheeks, which helps them (C)[get / getting] through
the winter. Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts
and flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to
find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful
eye, as predators are never too far away. They may
need to quickly escape back down into their holes,
which are complex structures stretching under the
ground. Despite urban areas generally having a
negative effect on wildlife, cities can actually provide
islands of protection for it.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)          (B)          (C)
solution: (A) 부사절 접속사 while 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 절이 와야 하나 뒤에 다른 동사(구)가 없으므로 주어를 이끄는 동명사 가 쓰일 수 없고, 주어 없이 동사구를 이룰 수도 없으므로, 접속 사를 남겨둔 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 주절 주어와 동일 한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 they가 some hamsters(어떤 햄스터 들)를 가리키며, ‘찾는’ 주체이고, ‘look for ~(~을 찾다)’의 look은 자동사이므로, 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 looking이 알맞다. (B) how 이하는 동사 See의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므로 의문 부사 how 뒤에 ‘주어+동사’의 평서문 어순을 이루는 it is가 알맞다. (C) 동사 helps와 목적어인 대명사 them에 이어져 ‘help+목적 어+목적격보어’(~가 …하도록 돕다)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목 적격보어 자리로, help는 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사 를 취하는 동사이므로 동사원형 get이 알맞다.

Jo: Then what happens after they arrive there?
Weidensaul: They regrow their digestive organs and
spend the summer (A)[feed / feeding] again,
and they undergo the same journey back to
Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to
30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By
the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown
close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
Jo: That’s truly impressive. By the way, I hear you’ve
visited Korea several times before. Why do you
come here so often?
Weidensaul: As a bird watcher and conservationist, I
find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and
China very special. They are some of the largest
tidal mudflats on the earth and (B)[provide /
providing] a critical stopover point for the
countless
migratory
birds
on
the
East
Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous
stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the
human eye, they ⓐ________________________________.
Jo: So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in
from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia?
Weidensaul: Yes. Many of these birds fly several
thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea.
Here, they have to double their weight in less
than two weeks and make another flight of
several thousand kilometers up north. That’s why
the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It’s one
of the few places in the world where migratory
birds can get the resources (C)[that / what] they
need on their difficult journey.
*East Asian-Australasian Flyway: 동아시아-대양주 철새 이동 경로

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)            (B)           (C)
solution: (A) 동사 spend와 시간 명사구 the summer에 이어지고 있으므 로, ‘~하면서 (시간)을 보내다’라는 뜻의 ‘spend+시간+-ing’ 구 문을 이루는 -ing 형태의 feeding이 알맞다. (B) 주어 They에 이어지는 복수동사 are와 등위접속사 and로 병렬연결을 이루어야 하며, 뒤에 목적어인 a critical stopover point가 이어지므로 능동태 복수동사인 provide가 알맞다. (C) 타동사 need의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they ~ journey)을 이끌어 선행사인 the resources를 수식하는 관계사 절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. 참고 로, 관계대명사 what은 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것(들)’이라는 뜻 으로 불완전한 절을 이끈다.

body:
Jo: Your new book says every spring and fall,
hundreds of millions to billions of migratory
birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to have
no idea ⓐthat it’s happening. Why is that?
Weidensaul: Well, most birds migrate after dark,
ⓑincluding almost all of the birds that are
normally active during the day. That’s ⓒwhy
it’s hard for us to realize the migration is
happening. They migrate at night because the
night sky is cooler, and ⓓthe air calmer. Besides,
there are fewer predators at night. If you could
strip away the night sky and make everything
visible, this migration would probably be the
largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
Jo: Among those global travelers in your book, I
found the bar-tailed godwits ⓔto be particularly
impressive.
Weidensaul: Sure. Some of them can even make a
10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific
Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in
11 days.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

there are times at night when a massive
migration happens right over your heads? The
scale of migration involving billions of birds
traveling up to thousands of kilometers (B)[leave
/ leaves] you in awe. On today’s Jo’s Tea Time,
we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul
to share his knowledge. He’s spent decades
(C)[to study / studying] migratory birds, writing
about them, and engaging in conservation
efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
Weidensaul: Thanks for having me, Jo.
(A)           (B)             (C)

solution: (A) 뒤에 단수가산명사구 neat trick이 이어지므로, ‘또 하나의 ~’라는 뜻으로 단수가산명사(구)를 수식하는 Another가 알맞 다. 참고로, other는 ‘다른 ~(들)’의 뜻으로 뒤에 복수가산명사 (구)나 불가산명사(구)가 이어진다. (B) and로 이어진 절에서 더 이상 몸무게가 늘지 않는다는 내용이 현재시제(can’t)로 진술되어 있으며 그 이전의 과거 시점부터 기준이 되는 현재 시점까지 먹을 수 있는 한 많이 먹은 상태라는 의미가 되어야 하므로, 현재완료(have[has]+p.p.)를 이루는 have가 알맞다. (C) because가 이끄는 절의 주어 these가 ‘their digestive organs(그들의 소화 기관들)’를 가리키며, ’활용되는‘ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사 to와 명사 use가 이어지므로, ‘put ~ to use(~을 활용하다)’의 수동태인 ‘be put to use(~가 활용되 다)’를 이루는 be put이 알맞다.

Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding
in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities,
Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people,
but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m
looking for is probably one of Europe’s most
critically endangered mammals.
Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try to
see some hamsters because this is one of the best
times of day to see them. At this time of the day,
there’s nobody around so they don’t have to avoid
people while (A)[looked / looking] for food. These
little ones have been in the area for decades, but
now live among the dead because development has
robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how (B)[is
it / it is] trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters
can pack a quarter of their body weight inside their
cheeks, which helps them (C)[get / getting] through
the winter. Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts
and flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle
wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to
find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to
the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful
eye, as predators are never too far away. They may
need to quickly escape back down into their holes,
which are complex structures stretching under the
ground. Despite urban areas generally having a
negative effect on wildlife, cities can actually provide
islands of protection for it.

Today, I’m looking for a tiny animal that’s hiding in one of Europe’s most beautiful capital cities, Vienna. Now it’s home to nearly 2 million people, but 50% of the city is green space. What I’m looking for is probably one of Europe’s most critically endangered mammals. Now, I’ve come really early to a graveyard to try to see some hamsters because this is one of the best times of day to see them. At this time of the day, there’s nobody around so they don’t have to avoid people while looking for food. These little ones have been in the area for decades, but now live among the dead because development has robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit. Look! I just found one over there. See how it is trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack a quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks, which helps them get through the winter. Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to find in graveyards. Even though the hamsters here have adapted to the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful eye, as predators are never too far away. They may have to escape quickly into their burrows, which are complex structures that extend underground. Despite urban areas generally having a negative effect on wildlife, cities can actually provide islands of protection for it.

What are the specific types of predators that threaten hamsters in Vienna?

3. 따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

choices: What’s your opinion on a sequel?
Could you clarify what a sequel is?
Could you tell me what a sequel is?
Could you elaborate on the term “a sequel”?
solution: Rick Riordan의 모험 소설 「The Lightning Thief」를 바탕으로 영화가 만들어졌다는 소년의 말에 소녀가 속편도 제작되었다 고 답하자 소년이 속편(sequel)의 뜻을 이해하지 못해 ‘What do you mean by a sequel?’(속편이 무슨 뜻이야?)이라고 물었 으며, 이에 소녀가 그것이 이전 영화의 이야기를 이어가는 또 다른 영화를 뜻한다고 설명하는 흐름이므로, 상대방의 의견을 묻는 표현인 ❷ ‘What’s your opinion on a sequel?‘(속편에 대 한 너의 생각은 무엇이니?)과는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘What do you mean by ~?’는 ‘~가 무슨 뜻이야?’라는 뜻으로, 상대방이 한 말 중 이해하지 못한 단어나 표현의 의미를 묻거 나 더 명확한 설명을 요청할 때 쓴다.

Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries ⓐincorporating the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered ⓑimportantly. The Temple
of the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, ⓒwhat
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
ⓓDepicting as a blonde woman wearing a golden
scarf and a golden crown, Saule lived in a palace at
the end of the sea, where she tended a garden of
golden apples. Saule would ride across the sky in a
chariot pulled by two tireless white horses. Saule
was not the only solar god to ride a vehicle across
the sky. The Greek gods Helios and Apollo were
both shown riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.

world’s most enduring myths. That is because there

“You have spoken well,” said Hermes, “and you

At this, the husband glanced over at old Baucis
with her thin, gray hair and her rough hands.
Baucis said, “We have lived together for many
years, and in all that time never has there been a
word of anger between us. Now, at last, we are
growing old and our long companionship is coming
to an end. Grant us this one request, that when we
come to die, we may ⓐperish in the same hour, so
that neither of us would be left without the other.”
She looked at Philemon, and he nodded in
approval, so the old couple turned their eyes on
the gods. “It shall be as you desire,” said Hermes.
“Few would have made such a good and moderate
request.”
Before long, the house became a temple, and the
neighbors, amazed at the change, often came to
ⓑworship and left offerings for the gods. For many
years, Baucis and Philemon lived in peace, passing
from old to extreme old age. At last, they were so
old and bowed that it seemed they could only walk
if they ⓒclung to each other. One evening, it took
them longer than ever to reach the usual spot they
would visit every day to look at the temple. There
they held each other’s arms, thinking that it was
perhaps the last time their limbs would ⓓsupport
them. As they stood, each one felt the other
change and only had time to turn and say

completely. Now there stood two tall trees growing

They swayed in the passing breeze as if they

M: Daedalus and his son Icarus were kept in a tall
tower by King Minos. To escape from the tower,
Daedalus made two pairs of giant wings out of
wax and feathers. As he attached the wings to
his son, he gave a warning. Flying too near the
ocean would make the wings wet and make
them too heavy to use. Flying too close to the
sun, the heat would melt the wax, and the wings
would fall apart. In either case, they surely would
die. Therefore, the key to their escape would be
in keeping to the middle. With the instructions
clear, both men left from the tower. They were
the first men ever to fly. While Daedalus flew
safely between the sun and the ocean, Icarus
was so excited that he forgot his father’s warning.
Daedalus could only watch in horror as Icarus flew
up higher and higher, powerless to change his
son’s fate. When the heat from the sun melted
the wax on his wings, Icarus fell from the sky.

body:
Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered important. The Temple of
the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.

을 가꾸며 살았다. Saule would ride across the sky
in a chariot pulled by two tireless white horses.
Saule was not the only solar god to ride a vehicle
across the sky. The Greek gods Helios and Apollo
were both shown riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because there
would be no life without that immense force in the
sky.

body:
Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered important. The Temple of
the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented by
Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
(A)황금 스카프와 황금 왕관을 쓴 금발 여인으로 묘사
된 Saule는 바다 끝에 있는 궁전에서 황금 사과 정원
을 가꾸며 살았다. Saule would ride across the sky
in a chariot pulled by two tireless white horses.
Saule was not the only solar god to ride a vehicle
across the sky. The Greek gods Helios and Apollo
were both shown riding chariots through the
heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because there
would be no life without that immense force in the

Ancient cultures recognized the sun’s power to
sustain life, so it was held in a place of honor in
most mythologies.
The Incas who lived in modern day Peru from the
12th to 16th centuries incorporated the sun in
many aspects of their culture, from holidays to
agriculture. Their sun god, Inti, was one of their
most powerful gods. (A) The Incan royal family was
said to be directly descended from Inti, so his
temples were considered important. (B) The Temple
of the Sun, in the capital city Cuzco, was made of
carved stone and filled with luxurious gold objects.
(C) In Baltic mythology, the sun was represented
by Saule, the mother and ruler of the world, who
determined the well-being of all life on the earth.
(D) Moreover, Baltic mythology was formed and
developed over generations, being passed down
through folk songs, legends, and oral storytelling
rather than written records. (E) Depicted as a blonde
woman wearing a golden scarf and a golden crown,
Saule lived in a palace at the end of the sea,
where she tended a garden of golden apples. Saule
would ride across the sky in a chariot pulled by
two tireless white horses. Saule was not the only
solar god to ride a vehicle across the sky. The
Greek gods Helios and Apollo were both shown
riding chariots through the heavens.
The Egyptian sun god Ra was said to ride in a
solar boat during the day. At night, he sailed
underwater until he returned to the sky in the east.
The sun has been a central figure in some of the
world’s most enduring myths. That is because

body:
Long ago, two strangers traveled through a certain
district, asking for food and shelter as they went.
For a long time, they found nothing but refusals
from both the rich and the poor. (A) Finally, they
came to a little cottage where a poor old couple,
Baucis and Philemon, lived. (B) The two had little to
offer since they lived entirely from the produce of
their small piece of land, a goose, and a few goats
and pigs. (C) They pulled their chairs forward for
their guests. (D) Philemon put a piece of broken
pot under one table leg, and Baucis rubbed the
table top with fresh mint and set some water over
the fire. (E) They set out their best delicacies on
the table. There were fresh vegetables baked over
the fire as well as wine. There was a big bowl in
the middle of the table to mix the wine with water.
